survey: A cowboy lasso (lariat) seen from the front, lying flat against a purple background. Parts: (1) A coil of rope on the left, about four turns, bound at the top with a red tie of rope or cord. (2) A straight tail that drops from the bottom of the coil and ends in a cream whipped or capped end. That end is fine. (3) A short length of rope that leaves the coil's lower right and runs into (4) a cream ring-shaped honda (the eye). (5) A large open loop on the right that starts and ends at the honda. The whole object floats against the backdrop with no surface. That fits an icon card, so it is not an error.

errors.where: Honda and large loop, right side
errors.what: The loop is drawn as a closed ring joined into the honda. In a real lasso the honda is tied at the rope's end and the standing part slides through it to form an adjustable loop. Here no rope passes through the eye: the rope from the coil and both ends of the loop all end inside the honda. The loop could not slide or tighten, so the lasso cannot work.

errors.where: Bottom of the coil, where the tail leaves
errors.what: The tail bends sharply out of the middle of the coil's lower turns and melts into them. It does not peel off the outermost turn, so you cannot tell which strand it continues.

errors.where: Coil turns, and where the rope leaves for the honda
errors.what: The coil's turns blend into one another and have no clear start or end. The rope that runs to the honda grows out of the coil's side without coming off a single traceable turn.

fix: A classic cowboy lariat. The rope ends in a small honda (eye) knot, and the standing part of the rope passes through the honda to form a large adjustable running loop. One continuous rope: the loop's rope runs through the eye and goes on into the neat coil. Each coil turn is distinct, and the free tail comes off the outermost turn of the coil and ends in a whipped tip.
